desc:
A steel rod has an integer length n = prices.length. A piece of length i (for 1 ≤ i ≤ n) sells for prices[i - 1], and the prices need not grow with the length. You may cut the rod into any number of pieces of integer length, and you may also sell it uncut.

Every single cut costs fee, whatever its position. Cutting a rod into m pieces therefore costs (m - 1) * fee. Return the largest possible profit, that is the total selling price of all pieces minus the cutting fees.

prices = [1,5,8,9,10,17,17,20], fee = 0 -> 22   (lengths 2 + 6)
prices = [1,5,8,9,10,17,17,20], fee = 1 -> 21   (22 - 1 for the single cut)
prices = [1,5,8,9,10,17,17,20], fee = 3 -> 20   (selling it whole beats every cut)
hints: Look at the first piece you cut off the left end of the rod. What is left over once it is gone?
Let best[L] be the best profit for a rod of length L. Either sell it whole, or cut off a first piece of length j (price prices[j - 1]), pay one fee, and then solve the remaining rod of length L - j.
best[L] = max(prices[L - 1], max over 1 ≤ j < L of prices[j - 1] - fee + best[L - j]). Fill L from 1 up to n and return best[n].
editorial: Every rod length is a smaller copy of the same question, so define best[L] as the maximum profit for a rod of length L (fees included). For a given L there are two kinds of plans. Either the rod is sold whole, giving prices[L - 1], or at least one cut is made. In the second case look at the leftmost piece, say of length j. It earns prices[j - 1], the cut that separates it from the rest costs fee, and the remaining L - j units are an independent smaller problem worth best[L - j].

So best[L] = max(prices[L - 1], max(prices[j - 1] - fee + best[L - j])) for 1 ≤ j < L. Charging the fee exactly when a first piece is cut away counts every cut once, because a plan with m pieces is built from exactly m - 1 such first-piece steps. This is an unbounded knapsack in disguise: the 'items' are the piece lengths 1..n, they can be used any number of times, and the capacity is the rod length. Time is O(n²), space O(n).
